advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the AST probe in `_llm_helpers_with_env_arg` to also consider `node.args.posonlyargs`/`node.args.kwonlyargs` (or assert no `_llm_*` env resolver uses them) so a keyword-only `env_name` cannot slip past the completeness guard.
evidence: `node.args.args` in Python's ast covers only positional-or-keyword params; `node.args.kwonlyargs` and `node.args.posonlyargs` are separate and not consulted here
All current helpers (`_llm_str`/`_llm_int`/`_llm_float`, config.py:426/439/459) use plain positional params, so this is latent, not a live failure
advisory.finding: The durable-guard test's AST probe collects only `node.args.args`, which excludes keyword-only and positional-only parameters. A future `_llm_*` resolver declaring `env_name` as keyword-only (after `*`) would be invisible to the completeness check and could yield a wrong positional index, silently reintroducing the exact drop-a-knob failure mode this guard is meant to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Build the parameter list from `node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.args` for indexing, and additionally verify `env_name` is not keyword-only (or explicitly fail if it is, since the scanner only reads positional args).
